notAMutation.finding: The first version of the Android drag guard was a vertical flick, and it PASSED (`a drag that starts on the row is a scroll, not a press (10 -> 10)`, real-input:android:--control:form, tree 06fc809409d7) with the Form row's touch-slop rule switched off. A list that can scroll intercepts the touch and answers the row with `ACTION_CANCEL`, so the flick never reaches the row's own decision — the guard had no teeth against this library's code. It now also asserts the list really moved, and a sideways drag (which no vertical container intercepts) is the one the slop rule answers. Same mutation, row 4, turns that red.
